result.title: MambaLIFT: Reference-Based Mechanism-Aware Attribution for VMamba
result.summary: Attributing predictions of visual state-space models remains challenging because input-dependent selective dynamics couple feature selection, recurrent state propagation, and shared computational pathways. We introduce MambaLIFT, a reference-based, multiplier-first attribution framework for VMamba that propagates contributions through its computational graph using interaction-aware rules for selective-scan injection, recurrent memory, LayerNorm, and shared pathways. MambaLIFT decomposes the reference-relative class-logit difference, \(f_c(x)-f_c(x^0)\), by spatial position, VSS block, scan direction, and computational mechanism. Experiments on ImageNet-1K evaluate VMamba-T and VMamba-B, with hyperparameters selected on a calibration set and faithfulness assessed on a disjoint held-out evaluation set. MambaLIFT achieves numerical conservation to floating-point precision across audited attribution interfaces in both configurations. Under mean-colour pixel flipping, it achieves significantly higher mean faithfulness scores than MambaLRP on both configurations and the highest scores among the evaluated methods, including Integrated Gradients with matched references. Under blurred replacement, MambaLIFT is non-inferior to MambaLRP on VMamba-T and equivalent on VMamba-B, indicating that its advantage depends on the replacement protocol. Ablations on VMamba-T show that interaction allocation, temporal propagation, and pathway composition affect attribution maps. Mechanism-level analyses further show that exact relevance conservation does not imply additive effects under finite interventions: the mechanism decomposition accounts for the reference-relative logit difference but does not estimate intervention effects or establish causal validity.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MambaLIFT，一个面向 VMamba 的参考基、乘性优先归因框架，把参考相对类 logit 差按空间位置、VSS 块、扫描方向和计算机制分解，并在 ImageNet-1K 上以像素替换下的忠实度等指标评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对选择性扫描、循环状态传播与共享通路的贡献分解，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的归因思路；文中亦明确机制分解不等于干预因果效应，可作为因果归因主张的边界参考。
